To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the calcium, magnesium and phosphorus concentrations in sheep foetal plasma are usually higher than in maternal juglar plasma.
the concentrations of calcium, phosphorus and magnesium in foetal and maternal plasma and in amniotc and allantoic fluids of sheep during the last eight week of pregnancy were variable.
the concentrations of calcium, and magnesium were greater in foetal than in maternal blood during the last 8 weeks of gestation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of calcium in the sheep conceptus.
the distribution of calcium and phosphorus within the foetal and maternal compartments of the pregnant ewe.

the transport of calcium and phosphorus across the placenta, the distribution of these ions within the conceptus and the possible involvement of magnesium in the regulation of the calcium and phosphorus economy of the foetal sheep.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium and magnesium values of foetal and maternal fluids were not in agreement with the hypothesis that foetal fluids were the major source of these minerals for foetal growth.
there is little or no evidence of transplacental calcium, magnesium and phosphorus transport in sheep.

the distribution of calcium and magnesium within the conceptus is similar to the distribution of these elements in other species and that the foetal concentrations of these elements reflect the maternal concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the foetal plasma calcium and magnesium concentrations are higher than maternal plasma concentrations and are not influenced by changes in maternal plasma values.
the calcium and magnesium distribution in sheep conceptuses is similar to that of the human foetus.

the foetal plasma concentrations of calcium and magnesium are higher and those of inorganic phosphorus lower than maternal plasma values, whereas in amniotic and allantoic fluids the reverse is true for calcium and magnesium and the phosphorus values are variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium and magnesium levels are higher in foetal than maternal plasma.
there is no clear evidence that calcium and magnesium concentrations in foetal and maternal fluids are regulated by the conceptus.
the calcium and magnesium homeostasis of the foetus is maintained independently from that of the ewe and that the foetus is capable of regulating its own concentrations of these minerals.
